cues.en: Hi.
cues.zh: 你好。

cues.en: So I sometimes see people saying things like... Okay. So your argument is that at some point in the future, we're going to develop intelligent agents that are able to reason about the world in general and take actions in the world to achieve their goals. These agents might have superhuman intelligence that allows them to be very good at achieving their goals, and this is a problem because they might have different goals from us.
cues.zh: 我有时会看到人们这样说……好，所以你的论点是：未来某个时候，我们会开发出智能体，它们能够对世界进行一般性推理，并在世界中采取行动来实现目标。这些智能体可能拥有超人类智能，使它们非常擅长实现自己的目标，而这就是问题所在，因为它们的目标可能和我们不同。

cues.en: But don't we kind of have that already?
cues.zh: 但我们不是已经有点这种东西了吗？

cues.en: Corporations can be thought of as superintelligent agents. They're able to think about the world in general, and they can outperform individual humans across a range of cognitive tasks.
cues.zh: 公司可以被看作超级智能体。它们能够对世界进行一般性思考，并且在一系列认知任务上能超越单个个人。

cues.en: And they have goals, namely maximizing profits or shareholder value or whatever. And those goals aren't the same as the overall goals of humanity.
cues.zh: 而且它们有目标，也就是最大化利润、股东价值之类的目标。而这些目标和人类的整体目标并不相同。

cues.en: So corporations are a kind of misaligned superintelligence. The people who say this, having established the metaphor, at this point tend to diverge mostly along political lines. Some say Corporations are therefore a clear threat to human values and goals in the same way that misaligned superintelligences are, and they need to be much more tightly controlled, if not destroyed altogether. Others say Corporations are like misaligned superintelligences,
cues.zh: 所以公司是一种目标错位的超级智能。说这话的人一旦建立了这个比喻，到这一步往往会主要沿着政治立场产生分歧。有些人说，因此公司就像目标错位的超级智能一样，明显威胁人类的价值和目标，需要被更严格地控制，甚至彻底摧毁。另一些人说，公司就像目标错位的超级智能，

cues.en: but corporations have been instrumental in the huge increases in human wealth and well-being that we've seen over the last couple of centuries with pretty minor negative side effects overall.
cues.zh: 但公司在过去几个世纪人类财富和福祉的巨大增长中发挥了关键作用，而总体负面副作用相当小。

cues.en: If that's the effect of misaligned superintelligences,
cues.zh: 如果这就是超级智能失调带来的后果，

cues.en: I don't see why we should be concerned about AI. And others say Corporations certainly have their problems, but we seem to have developed systems that keep them under control well enough that they're able to create value and do useful things without literally killing everyone.
cues.zh: 我不明白为什么我们要担心AI。还有人说，企业确实有它们的问题，但我们似乎已经发展出了一套系统，能足够好地控制它们，使它们能够创造价值、做有用的 things，而不会真的把所有人都杀掉。

cues.en: So perhaps we can learn something about how to control or align superintelligences
cues.zh: 所以也许我们可以从中学到一些关于如何控制或对齐超级智能的东西，

cues.en: by looking at how we handle corporations. So, we're gonna let the first two fight amongst themselves,
cues.zh: 通过观察我们如何管理企业。那么，我们让前两个自己打起来，

cues.en: and we'll talk to the third guy. So how good is this metaphor? Are corporations really like misaligned artificial general super intelligences?
cues.zh: 然后我们跟第三个人谈。那么这个比喻有多好？企业真的像失调的人工通用超级智能吗？

cues.en: Quick note before we start, we're going to be comparing corporations
cues.zh: 开始之前快速说明一下，我们要把企业

cues.en: to AI systems and this gets a lot more complicated when you consider that corporations in fact use AI systems. So for the sake of simplicity,
cues.zh: 比作AI系统，而当你考虑到企业实际上在使用AI系统时，这就变得复杂多了。所以为了简单起见，

cues.en: we're going to assume that corporations don't use AI systems because otherwise the problem gets recursive
cues.zh: 我们假设企业不使用AI系统，因为否则问题就会变成递归的

cues.en: and like not in a cool way. First off, are corporations agents in the relevant way?
cues.zh: 而且不是那种酷的方式。首先，企业在相关意义上算是智能体吗？

cues.en: I would say, yeah, pretty much. I think that it's reasonably productive to think of a corporation as an agent. They do seem to make decisions and take actions in the world in order to achieve goals in the world. But I think you face a similar problem thinking of corporations as agents as you do when you try to think of human beings as agents. In economics, it's common to model human beings as agents that want to maximize their money in some sense. And you can model corporations in the same way and this is useful,
cues.zh: 我会说，是的，差不多。我认为把企业看作一个智能体是相当有成效的。它们确实似乎会做决策并在世界上采取行动，以实现世界上的目标。但我认为，把企业看作智能体时你会遇到一个类似的问题，就像你试图把人看作智能体时一样。在经济学中，常见做法是把人建模为在某种意义上想要最大化自己金钱的智能体。你可以用同样的方式建模企业，这很有用，

cues.en: but it is kind of a simplification
cues.zh: 但这算是一种简化

cues.en: in that human beings in practice want things that aren't just money. And while corporations are more directly aligned with profit maximizing than individual human beings are, it's not quite that simple. So yes, we can think of corporations as agents,
cues.zh: 因为实际上人想要的不只是钱。虽然企业比个人更直接地与利润最大化对齐，但事情并没有那么简单。所以是的，我们可以把企业看作智能体，

cues.en: but we can't treat their stated goals as being exactly equivalent to their actual goals in practice. More on that later. So corporations are more or less agents.
cues.zh: 但我们不能把它们声称的目标等同于它们实际上的目标。这个后面再说。所以企业或多或少算是智能体。

cues.en: Are they generally intelligent agents?
cues.zh: 它们通常是智能体吗？

cues.en: Again, yeah, I think so. I mean, corporations are made up of human beings. So they have all the same general intelligence capabilities that human beings have. So then the question is, are they super intelligent?
cues.zh: 再说一次，我认为是。我的意思是，公司由人组成。所以，它们具备人类拥有的所有通用智能能力。那问题就变成了：它们是超级智能吗？

cues.en: This is where things get interesting because the answer is kind of. Like, SpaceX is able to design a better rocket than any individual human engineer could design. Rocket design is a cognitive task, and SpaceX is better at that than any human being. Therefore, SpaceX is a superintelligence
cues.zh: 有意思的地方就在这里，因为答案算是吧。比如，SpaceX 能设计出比任何单个人类工程师都更好的火箭。火箭设计是一项认知任务，而 SpaceX 在这方面比任何人类都强。因此，SpaceX 是火箭设计领域的超级智能

cues.en: in the domain of rocket design.
cues.zh: 智能体。

cues.en: But a calculator is a superintelligence in the domain of arithmetic. That's not enough. Are corporations general superintelligences?
cues.zh: 但计算器是算术领域的超级智能。这还不够。公司是通用超级智能吗？

cues.en: Do they outperform humans across a wide range of cognitive tasks as an AGI could? In practice, it depends on the task.
cues.zh: 它们能像 AGI 一样，在广泛的认知任务上胜过人类吗？实际上，这取决于具体任务。

cues.en: Consider playing a strategy game.
cues.zh: 比如玩策略游戏。

cues.en: For the sake of simplicity, let's use a game that humans still beat AI systems at, like Starcraft.
cues.zh: 为简单起见，我们选一款人类目前仍然胜过 AI 系统的游戏，比如 Starcraft。

cues.en: If a corporation for some reason had to win at Starcraft,
cues.zh: 如果一家公司因为某种原因必须在 Starcraft 中获胜，

cues.en: it could perform about as well as the best human players.
cues.zh: 它的表现可以和顶尖人类玩家差不多。

cues.en: It would do that by hiring the best human players.
cues.zh: 它会通过雇用顶尖人类玩家来做到这一点。

cues.en: But you won't achieve superhuman play that way. A human player acting on behalf of a corporation is just a human player,
cues.zh: 但这样无法实现超人的游戏水平。代表公司行动的人类玩家，本质上仍然只是一个人类玩家，

cues.en: and the corporation doesn't really have a way to do much better than that. A team of reasonably good Starcraft players working together to control one army will still lose to a single very good player working alone. This seems to be true for a lot of strategy games. The classic example is the game of Kasparov versus the world,
cues.zh: 而公司实际上没有办法做得比这更好。由一群水平不错的 Starcraft 玩家合作控制一支军队，仍然会输给一个单独行动的顶尖玩家。很多策略游戏似乎都是这样。经典例子就是 Kasparov 对决全世界，

cues.en: where Gary Kasparov played against the entire rest of the world cooperating on the Internet.
cues.zh: Gary Kasparov 与互联网上合作的全世界其他人对弈。

cues.en: The game was kind of weird, but Kasparov ended up winning. And the kind of real world strategy that corporations have to do seems like it might be similar as well. When companies outsmart their competition, it's usually because they have a small number of decision makers who are unusually smart
cues.zh: 这游戏有点怪，但最终卡斯帕罗夫赢了。而企业在现实世界中不得不采用的策略，似乎也与之类似。当公司智胜竞争对手时，通常是因为它们有少数异常聪明的决策者，

cues.en: rather than because they have a 100 reasonably smart people working together. For at least some tasks, teams of humans are not able to effectively combine their intelligence to achieve highly superhuman performance.
cues.zh: 而不是因为有一百个还算聪明的人在一起合作。至少在某些任务上，人类团队无法有效整合各自的智慧来实现高度超人的表现。

cues.en: So corporations are limited to around human level intelligence at those tasks. To break down why this is, let's look at some different options corporations have for ways to combine human intelligences.
cues.zh: 所以，在这些任务上，企业受限于人类水平的智能。为了剖析原因，我们来看看企业整合人类智慧的一些不同方式。

cues.en: One obvious way is specialization.
cues.zh: 一个显而易见的方式是专业化。

cues.en: If you can divide the task into parts that people can specialize in, you can outperform individuals.
cues.zh: 如果你能把任务拆分成人们可以专攻的部分，你就能超越个体。

cues.en: You can have one person who's skilled at engine design, one who's great at aerodynamics, one who knows a lot about structural engineering, and one who's good at
cues.zh: 你可以让一个人擅长引擎设计，一个人精通空气动力学，一个人对结构工程了解很深，还有一个人擅长

cues.en: avionics.
cues.zh: 航空电子。

cues.en: Can you tell I'm not a rocket surgeon? Anyway, if these people with their different skills are able to work together well with each person doing what they're best at, the resulting agent will, in a sense, have superhuman intelligence.
cues.zh: 看得出我不是火箭外科医生吧？总之，如果这些拥有不同技能的人能够良好协作，每个人做自己最擅长的事，那么由此产生的智能体在某种意义上就拥有了超人的智能。

cues.en: No single human could ever be so good at so many different things.
cues.zh: 没有任何一个单一的人能在这么多不同的事情上都如此出色。

cues.en: But this mechanism doesn't get you superhumanly high intelligence,
cues.zh: 但这种机制并不能带来超人般的高智力，

cues.en: just superhumanly
cues.zh: 只是超人般的

cues.en: broad intelligence,
cues.zh: 广泛智能，

cues.en: whereas superintelligence
cues.zh: 而超级智能

cues.en: software AGI might look like this.
cues.zh: 软件 AGI 可能会是这个样子的。

cues.en: So specialization
cues.zh: 因此，专业化分工

cues.en: yields a fairly limited form of superintelligence
cues.zh: 带来的超级智能其实相当有限，

cues.en: if you can split your task up. But that's not easy for all tasks.
cues.zh: 前提是你得能把任务拆解开来。但并非所有任务都容易拆解。

cues.en: For example, the task of coming up with creative ideas or strategies isn't easy to split up. You either have a good idea or you don't. But as a team, you can get everyone to suggest a strategy or idea and then pick the best one. That way a group can perform better than any individual human. How much better though? And how does that change with the size of the team? I got curious about exactly how this works, so I came up with a toy model. Now I'm not a statistician, I'm a computer scientist. So rather than working it out properly, I just simulated it a 100,000,000 times because that was quicker. Okay. So here's the idea quality distribution for an individual human. We'll model it as a normal distribution with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 20. So what this means is you ask a human for a suggestion and sometimes they do really well and come up with a 130 level strategy.
cues.zh: 比如，构思创意或策略的任务就不容易拆解。你要么有点子，要么没有。但作为团队，你可以让每个人都提一个策略或想法，然后选出最好的那一个。这样一来，团队的表现就能胜过任何单个人类。不过到底能强多少？这又会如何随团队规模变化？我很好奇这其中的运作逻辑，于是建了一个玩具模型。我不是统计学家，我是计算机科学家。所以与其去严谨地推导数学公式，我直接跑了一亿次仿真，因为这样更快。好，这是单个人类的创意质量分布。我们把它建模为均值 100、标准差 20 的正态分布。这意味着，如果你向一个人征求建议，有时他们发挥超常，能提出 130 分水平的策略。

cues.en: Sometimes they screw up and can only give you a 70 idea, but most of the time it's around a 100. Now suppose we had a second person whose intelligence is the same as the first.
cues.zh: 有时他们会搞砸，只能给出 70 分的想法，但大多数时候都在 100 分左右。现在假设我们有第二个人，智力和第一个人一样。

cues.en: We have both of them come up with ideas and we keep whichever idea is better.
cues.zh: 我们让两人各自提出想法，然后保留更好的那个。

cues.en: The resulting team of two people combined looks like this. On average, the ideas are better. The mean is now, what, a 107?
cues.zh: 合并后的两人团队看起来是这样。平均来说，想法更好了。均值现在是，大概 107？

cues.en: And as we keep adding people, the performance gets better. Here's five people,
cues.zh: 随着我们不断加人，表现会越来越好。这是五个人，
10 个人，

cues.en: 20, 50, a 100. Remember, these are probability distributions. So the height doesn't really matter. The point is that the distributions move to the right and get thinner. The average idea quality goes up and the standard deviation goes down. So we're coming up with better ideas and more reliably.
cues.zh: 20、50、100。记住，这些是概率分布。所以高度其实不重要。关键是分布向右移动，而且变得更窄。平均想法质量上升，标准差下降。所以我们产生的想法更好，而且更稳定可靠。

cues.en: But you see how the progress is slowing down. We're using a 100 times as much brainpower here, but our average ideas are only like 25% better.
cues.zh: 但你能看到进展在放缓。我们这里用了 100 倍的脑力，但平均想法只好了大约 25%。

cues.en: What if we use a thousand people? 10 times more resources again only gets us up to around a 135,
cues.zh: 如果用一千个人呢？资源又多了 10 倍，也只把我们提升到大约 135，

cues.en: diminishing returns. So what does this mean for corporations?
cues.zh: 收益递减。那么这对公司意味着什么？

cues.en: Well, first off, to be fair, this team of a thousand people is clearly super intelligent. The worst ideas it ever has are still so good that an individual human will hardly ever manage to think of them. But it's still pretty limited. There's all this space off to the right of the graph that it would take vast team sizes to ever get into. If you're wondering how this would look with 7,000,000,000 humans, well, you have to work out the statistical solution yourself. The point is the team isn't that super intelligent because it's never going to think of an idea that no human could think of, which is kind of obvious when you think about it. But AGI isn't limited in that way. And in practice, even this model is way too optimistic for corporations. Firstly, because it assumes that the quality of suggestions for a particular problem is uncorrelated between humans, which is clearly not true. And secondly, because you have to pick out the best suggestion.
cues.zh: 先说清楚，公平地讲，这个一千人的团队显然超级智能。它想出的最差想法仍然好到单个人类几乎不可能想到。但它仍然相当有限。图上右侧还有一大片空间，要进入那里需要极其庞大的团队规模。如果你想知道 70 亿人类会是什么样，那得你自己去算统计解。关键是，这个团队并没有那么超级智能，因为它永远不会想到一个没有任何人类能想到的想法——仔细想想，这其实挺明显。但 AGI 不受这种限制。而在实践中，即便这个模型对公司来说也过于乐观了。首先，它假设针对某个问题的建议质量在人与人之间不相关，这显然不对。其次，因为你必须挑出最佳建议。

cues.en: But how can you be sure that you'll know the best idea when you see it? It happens to be true a lot of the time for a lot of problems that we care about that evaluating solutions is easier than coming up with them. You know, Homer, it's very easy to criticize.
cues.zh: 但你怎么能确定，看到最好的想法时你能认出来？对我们关心的很多问题来说，很多时候确实如此：评估解决方案比想出解决方案更容易。你知道，Homer，批评很容易。

cues.en: Fun too. Machine learning relies pretty heavily on this. Like writing a program that differentiates pictures of cats and dogs is really hard, but evaluating such a program is fairly simple. You just show it lots of pictures of cats and dogs and see how well it does. The clever bit is in figuring out how to take a method for evaluating solutions and use that to create good solutions. Anyway, this assumption isn't always true. And even when it is, the fact that evaluation is easier or cheaper than generation doesn't mean that evaluation is easy or cheap. Like, I couldn't generate a good rocket design myself, but I can tell you that this one needs work.
cues.zh: 也很有趣。机器学习很依赖这一点。比如写一个区分猫狗图片的程序很难，但评估这样的程序相当简单。你只要给它看很多猫狗图片，看它表现如何。巧妙之处在于，想办法利用评估解决方案的方法来生成好的解决方案。总之，这个假设并不总是成立。即使成立，评估比生成更容易或更便宜，也不代表评估就容易或便宜。比如，我自己设计不出好的火箭，但我能告诉你这个设计还需要改进。

cues.en: So evaluation is easier than generation.
cues.zh: 所以评估比生成更容易。

cues.en: But that's a very expensive way to find out, and I wouldn't have been able to do it the cheap way by just looking at the blueprints. The skills needed to evaluate in advance whether a given rocket design will explode are very closely related to the skills needed to generate a non exploding rocket design. So, yeah, even if a corporation could somehow get around being limited to the kind of ideas that humans are able to generate, they're still limited to the kind of ideas that humans are able to recognize as good ideas. Just how serious is this limitation?
cues.zh: 但这样发现的代价很高，而且我也没法只靠看蓝图就用便宜的方法做到。预先评估某个火箭设计会不会爆炸所需的技能，和生成不会爆炸的火箭设计所需的技能密切相关。所以，是的，即使一家公司能设法绕过“只能产生人类能想到的点子”的限制，它们仍然受限于“只能产生人类能识别为好点子的想法”。这个限制到底有多严重？

cues.en: How good are the strategies and ideas that corporations are missing out on? Well, take a minute to think of an idea that's too good for any human to recognize it as good.
cues.zh: 企业错失的策略和想法到底有多好？花一分钟想想一个好到没人能识别出来的点子。

cues.en: Got one?
cues.zh: 想到了吗？

cues.en: Well, it was worth a shot. We actually do have an example of this kind of thing in Move 37 from AlphaGo's 2016 match with world champion Lee Sedol. Is this kind of of evaluation
cues.zh: 好吧，值得一试。其实我们真有这样的例子，就是AlphaGo在2016年对阵世界冠军李世石时的第37手。这种评估

cues.en: value.
cues.zh: 价值。

cues.en: That's a very that's a very surprising move. I thought I thought it was I thought it was a mistake.
cues.zh: 那是一个非常非常令人惊讶的一步。我以为我以为那是个失误。

cues.en: Yeah. That turned out to be pretty much the move that won the game. But your go playing corporation is never going to make move 37.
cues.zh: 是啊。结果那几乎就是赢下比赛的那一步。但你们下围棋的企业永远不会走出第37手。

cues.en: Even if someone happens to suggest it, it's almost certainly not going to be chosen. Normally, human, we never play this one because
cues.zh: 即使有人碰巧提出来，也几乎肯定不会被执行。通常，人类从不这么下，因为

cues.en: it's bad. It's not enough for someone in your corporation to have a great idea. The people at the top need to recognize that it's a great idea. That means that there's a limit on the effective creative or strategic intelligence of a corporation which is determined by the intelligence of the decision makers and their ability to know a good idea when they see one. Okay. What about speed?
cues.zh: 这步很糟。企业里有人有好点子还不够，高层得能认出这是个好点子。这意味着企业的有效创造力或战略智能存在上限，这个上限由决策者的智能以及他们识别好点子的能力决定。好，那速度呢？

cues.en: That's one of the things that makes AI systems so powerful and one of the ways that software AGI is likely to be super intelligent. The general trend is we go from computers can't do this at all to computers can do this much faster than people. Not always, but in general. So I wouldn't be surprised if that pattern continues with AGI. How does a corporation rate on speed?
cues.zh: 这是让AI系统如此强大的原因之一，也是软件AGI可能超级智能的途径之一。总体趋势是，我们从计算机完全做不到，发展到计算机能比人快得多地做到。不总是如此，但总体上是这样。所以我不会惊讶这个模式在AGI上延续。企业在速度上表现如何？

cues.en: Again, it kind of depends. This is closely related to something we've talked about before, parallelizability.
cues.zh: 这还是要看情况。它和我们之前聊过的一个概念密切相关：可并行性。

cues.en: Some tasks are easy to split up and work on in parallel and some aren't.
cues.zh: 有些任务容易拆分并行处理，有些则不行。

cues.en: For example, if you've got a big list of a thousand numbers and you need to add them all up, it's very easy to parallelize. If you have 10 people, you can just say, okay, you take the first 100 numbers, you take the second 100, you take the third, and so on. Have everybody add up their part of the list, and then at the end, you add up everyone's totals. However long the list is, you can throw more people at it and get it done faster,
cues.zh: 比如，你有一个包含一千个数字的大列表，需要把它们全部加起来，这就很容易并行化。如果你有10个人，你可以直接说，好，你负责前100个数字，你负责第二个100个，你负责第三个，以此类推。让每个人把自己那部分加起来，最后再把每个人的总和加起来。不管列表多长，你都可以投入更多人，让它更快完成，

cues.en: much faster than any individual human could. This is the kind of task where it's easy for corporations to achieve superhuman speed. But suppose instead of summing a list, you have a simple simulation that you want to run for say a thousand seconds.
cues.zh: 比任何单个人都快得多。这类任务很容易让公司达到超人速度。但假设你不是在求和列表，而是要运行一个简单模拟，比如一千秒。

cues.en: You can't say, okay, you work out the first hundred seconds of the simulation, you do the next hundred, you do the next hundred and so on. Because obviously the person who's simulating second 100 needs to know what happened at the end of second 99 before they can get started. So this is what's called an inherently serial task.
cues.zh: 你不能说，好，你算模拟的前一百秒，你算接下来一百秒，再下一个一百秒，以此类推。因为显然，模拟第100秒的人需要知道第99秒结束时发生了什么，才能开始。这就是所谓的固有串行任务。

cues.en: You can't easily do it much faster by adding more people. You can't get a baby in less than nine months by hiring two pregnant women, you know. Most real world tasks are somewhere in between. You get some benefits from adding more people, but again, you hit diminishing returns.
cues.zh: 你没法通过加人轻松让它快很多。你没法靠雇两个孕妇不到九个月就生出孩子。现实世界大多数任务介于两者之间。加人会有一些好处，但同样会遇到收益递减。

cues.en: Some parts of the task can be split up and worked on in parallel. Some parts need to happen one after the other. So yes, corporations can achieve superhuman speed at some important cognitive tasks. But really, if you want to talk about speed in a principled way, you need to differentiate between throughput,
cues.zh: 任务的某些部分可以拆分并行处理，有些部分则必须按顺序进行。所以，企业确实能在一些重要认知任务上达到超人速度。但说真的，如果想有原则地讨论速度，就得区分吞吐量，

cues.en: how much goes through the system within a certain time, and latency,
cues.zh: 即在一定时间内通过系统的量，以及延迟，

cues.en: how long it takes a single thing to go through the system. These ideas are most often used in things like networking, and I think that's the easiest way to explain it. So basically, let's say you need to send someone a large file, and you can either send it over a dial up Internet connection or you can send them a physical disk through the postal system. The dial up connection is low latency.
cues.zh: 即单个事物通过系统所需的时间。这些概念最常用于网络传输等领域，我觉得这是最容易解释的方式。简单来说，假设你要给别人发一个大文件，你可以通过拨号上网发送，也可以通过邮政系统寄一块物理磁盘。拨号连接是低延迟的。

cues.en: Each bit of the file goes through the system quickly,
cues.zh: 文件的每一位都快速通过系统，

cues.en: but it's also low throughput. The rate at which you can send data is pretty low.
cues.zh: 但它的吞吐量也很低。你能发送数据的速率相当低。

cues.en: Whereas sending the physical disk is high latency, it might take days for the first bit to arrive, but it's also high throughput. You can put vast amounts of data on the disk, so your average data sent per second could actually be very good. Corporations are able to combine human intelligences
cues.zh: 而寄物理磁盘是高延迟的，第一位数据可能要几天才能到达，但它的吞吐量也很高。你可以把海量数据放在磁盘上，所以每秒平均发送的数据量其实可能非常好。企业能够结合人类智能

cues.en: to achieve superhuman throughput
cues.zh: 来实现超人的吞吐量

cues.en: so they can complete large complex tasks faster than individual humans could.
cues.zh: 因此它们能比单个人类更快地完成大型复杂任务。

cues.en: But the thing is, a system can't have lower latency than its slowest component
cues.zh: 但问题是，一个系统的延迟不可能低于它最慢的组件

cues.en: and corporations are made of humans, so corporations aren't able to achieve superhuman latency. And in practice, as you've no doubt experienced, it's quite the opposite. So corporate intelligence is kind of like sending the physical disk.
cues.zh: 而企业由人组成，所以企业无法达到超人级延迟。实践中，你肯定也经历过，情况恰恰相反。所以企业智能有点像寄送实体磁盘。

cues.en: Corporations can get a lot of cognitive work done in a given time, but they're slow to react.
cues.zh: 企业能在给定时间内完成大量认知工作，但反应很慢。

cues.en: And that's a big part of what makes corporations relatively controllable.
cues.zh: 而这正是企业相对可控的重要原因。

cues.en: They tend to react so slowly that even governments are sometimes able to move fast enough to deal with them. Software superintelligence is on the other hand, could have superhuman throughput and superhuman latency,
cues.zh: 它们往往反应太慢，以至于有时连政府都能行动得足够快，来应对它们。软件超级智能则不同，它可以拥有超人级吞吐量和超人级延迟，

cues.en: which is something we've never experienced before in a general intelligence.
cues.zh: 这是一般智能从未经历过的情况。

cues.en: So are corporations superintelligent agents?
cues.zh: 那么，企业是超级智能体吗？

cues.en: Well, they're pretty much generally intelligent agents,
cues.zh: 嗯，它们基本算是通用智能体，

cues.en: which are somewhat superintelligent in some ways and somewhat below human performance in others.
cues.zh: 在某些方面有点超级智能，在另一些方面又低于人类表现。

cues.en: So, yeah, kinda?
cues.zh: 所以，算吧？

cues.en: The next question is, are they misaligned?
cues.zh: 下一个问题是，它们目标错位了吗？

cues.en: But this video is already like fourteen and a half minutes long, so we'll get to that in the next video.
cues.zh: 但这个视频已经14分半了，我们下个视频再谈。

cues.en: I want to end the video by saying a big thank you to my excellent patrons. It's all of these people here. In this video, I'm especially thanking Pablo Eder or Pablo Ida. Nobody knows for sure. Recently, I've been putting a lot of time into some projects that I'm not able to talk about, but as soon as I can patrons will be the first to know. Thank you again so much for your generosity
cues.zh: 我想在视频结尾衷心感谢我优秀的赞助者。就是这里的这些人。本期我特别感谢 Pablo Eder，或者 Pablo Ida，没人确定。最近我投入了很多时间在一些不能谈论的项目上，但一旦能说，赞助者会最先知道。再次非常感谢你们的慷慨

cues.en: and thank you all for watching. I'll see you next time.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家观看。下次见。
